subject: Which SOC 2 package should we accept (expired vs reissued)?
messages:
From: Diane Park <security@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — which file should we accept?

Hi Tessa,

We ran the SOC 2 package you sent through procurement and they flagged a couple of things: the PDF we received lists an audit period ending on 2023-06-30 and is marked as "expired" in our tracker. Meanwhile, the vendor portal shows a different file name with a 2024 date. Can you confirm which of the files is the authoritative current Type II for Redwood?

Our security team needs to know whether we should accept the bridge letter you previously shared, or wait for a reissued Type II. If a reissue is coming, can you share an expected date and whether the reissued file will replace the current package or be an addendum?

We also need any short interim attestation we can attach to the procurement record so they can move forward with an exception if necessary.

Thanks — if easier, feel free to call; otherwise a short note here will work.

Best,
Diane Park
Security & Compliance Manager
AcmeHealth

Attachment: attached_file: SOC2_Type_package_received.pdf (pdf stub)
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Diane Park <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — which file should we accept?

Hi Diane — thanks for the note and sorry for the confusion. Short answer: you can accept the bridge letter as interim evidence today; we have a minor metadata reissue planned for the underlying Type II that will not change scope or control outcomes. Details below and I copied Marissa (audit liaison) and Soojin (security ops) to confirm.

What you likely received: SOC2_TypeII_20230630_v1.pdf — this is the originally issued package that covers the period 2022-07-01 through 2023-06-30 but the filename metadata has a legacy timestamp which made it look expired in your tracker.

Planned action: we will publish a corrected file (SOC2_TypeII_20230630_v2.pdf) that updates the Document ID and minor header fields. The audit period and findings are identical. Estimated reissue date: within 10–14 calendar days.

Interim evidence: we can provide a signed bridge letter and a one-page interim attestation that procurement can accept today while the final PDF is reissued. I attached the bridge and the draft attestation for review.

Next steps I propose:
- Acme confirms acceptance of bridge/attestation as interim evidence
- We trigger DocuSign for the attestation (I can send link)
- Marissa confirms the exact filename and confirms when the reissued PDF is uploaded

If you want the reissued PDF first, we can accelerate but procurement may hold for the signed attestation. Let me know which route you prefer.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Ops (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Bridge_20241115.pdf (pdf stub), interim-attestation-acme-20271116.pdf (pdf stub)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Diane Park <security@acmehealth.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 09:49:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request — which file should we accept? (audit liaison)

Hi Diane — Marissa here, I own SOC 2 packaging for Redwood. Wanted to add the audit-side details so procurement has the right acceptance criteria.

Clarifying the filenames and coverage: the underlying audited period is 2022-07-01 through 2023-06-30. The original package (filename ending in _v1.pdf) was published earlier this year but it contained a header field that failed our internal checksum (a non-substantive metadata value). That led to our security team issuing a corrected package (we'll publish _v2.pdf). The control testing, scope, and auditor attestation are the same — there is no change to control outcomes.

What you should accept today: the signed bridge letter (SOC2_Bridge_20241115.pdf) is acceptable interim evidence for procurement to approve an exception. If your policy *requires* a Type II PDF only, we can prioritize the reissue to be uploaded sooner and will confirm the exact filename when live.

Reissue timeline: internal QA completes tomorrow and our compliance team will publish the corrected PDF by 2027-11-28 at the latest. We'll push a release note and the exact file name to the shared folder and to your security contact.

DocuSign: we can either send the bridge/attestation via DocuSign to procurement or provide a digitally signed PDF with a timestamp. If procurement needs an envelope, click the DocuSign link I copied below and we will route it to the right approver.

Let me know if you want me to open a short formal exception (I can attach the attestation directly into the exception record).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_20230630_v1.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Diane Park <security@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request — which file should we accept?

Hi Marissa/Tessa — thanks for the fast clarification. Procurement will accept the signed bridge letter as interim evidence and will proceed with the exception while we wait for the reissued PDF. Please send the DocuSign envelope for the attestation to procurement@acmehealth.com and confirm the final filename when the corrected PDF is live so we can update our records.

Appreciate the quick turn.

Best,
Diane
